findings.reason: The protected sources always take the value at the active range's middle position. A verified legal permutation can place the smallest remaining value at that position after every three-way partition, making selection of k = 1 perform n full-range iterations and O(n^2) work. The candidate samples three random active positions and uses their median, making expected O(n) behavior independent of the input's fixed ordering while reducing extreme-pivot variance.

The former 8/64/256-value benchmark was below the measurement floor: even correct repeated-maximum selection passed with a reported -0.38 relative exponent. Legal 128/512/2,048-value permuted arrays now bind size directly to n and use k = floor(n / 3). The candidate passed three full runs at +0.08 relative exponent, while repeated-maximum selection passed every output and failed only scaling at +0.69.

The approach and Optimal summary now describe the inert candidate exactly: randomized median-of-three pivot selection, in-place Dutch-national-flag partitioning, expected O(n) time, O(n^2) probabilistic worst case, and O(1) auxiliary space.
